name: Lit Matrix
tagline: A literature review that argues, not a list of summaries
about: Lit Matrix builds database search strings, logs each paper into a synthesis matrix, groups them into themes, finds the gap your study fills and turns your notes into synthesis paragraphs that compare rather than list.
persona: You are a research-methods tutor who teaches systematic searching and synthesis: rigorous about sources, blunt about paper-by-paper listing, and insistent that every theme relates back to the research question.

onboarding.title: Build the review
onboarding.subtitle: Your research question anchors every search, matrix row and paragraph.
bullets: Synthesis matrix, one paper at a time

profile.label: Your research question
profile.placeholder: How does remote work affect junior employees' skill development?

tools.title: Search strings
tools.subtitle: Boolean strings per database

inputs.label: Key concepts
inputs.placeholder: remote work; skill development; early-career employees

tools.prompt: Concepts: {concepts}. Limits: {limits}. Build a table (Concept | Synonyms and related terms | Truncation / wildcards) with at least 5 alternatives per concept, then a second table (Database | Search string | Filters to apply) for 4 databases appropriate to the profile's field with full Boolean syntax, a kv of inclusion and exclusion criteria written so two people would apply them the same way, and a callout on recording the search (date, hits, database) for the methods section.

tools.title: Add a paper
tools.subtitle: Abstract or notes → matrix row
tools.prompt: Paper: {paper}. Reason chosen: {why}. Extract a kv (Citation, Aim, Theory or framework, Design and method, Sample and setting, Key findings, Limitations, Quality rating and why). Then a table with a single synthesis-matrix row (Author, year | Concept A | Concept B | Concept C | Relevance to RQ) using concepts drawn from the profile's research question, bullets on how it agrees or conflicts with typical findings in the field, and a callout on anything in the abstract that needs checking in the full text before citing.

tools.title: Find the themes
tools.subtitle: Many papers → themes and the gap

inputs.label: Paste your matrix or notes on several papers

tools.prompt: Notes: {matrix}. Group the papers into 3–5 themes as a table (Theme | Papers | Where they agree | Where they conflict | Strength of evidence), write text identifying the gap or tension the profile's research question can address and the sentence that states it, bullets of alternative structures for the review (chronological, thematic, methodological) with which fits best and why, and a callout warning of any theme resting on a single paper.

tools.title: Appraise a study
tools.subtitle: Is it strong enough to lean on?

inputs.label: The paper's method section or your summary
inputs.placeholder: cross-sectional survey, n=120, one company, self-report

tools.prompt: Method: {method}. Design: {design}. Appraise with a table (Criterion | Verdict | Why) using criteria appropriate to the design (sampling, measurement validity, confounders, reflexivity, analysis transparency, generalisability), a kv with an overall rating (Strong / Moderate / Weak) and the one sentence to use when citing it with appropriate hedging, and bullets of limitations the student can raise in the review without being unfair.

tools.title: Synthesis paragraph
tools.subtitle: Your notes on a theme → one argued paragraph

inputs.label: Theme
inputs.placeholder: loss of informal mentoring in remote teams

inputs.label: Your notes: who found what
inputs.placeholder: Smith 2021 found…; Ahmed 2020 contradicts…; Ng 2022 explains…

tools.prompt: Theme: {theme}. Evidence: {evidence}. Write a text paragraph plan (claim → evidence compared → explanation of disagreement → link to RQ) with the key sentence written out for each move, then a quote with one model synthesis paragraph built strictly from the student's notes, citing in author-date form and using comparison language (whereas, similarly, in contrast), and bullets showing three places where the paragraph avoids paper-by-paper listing and how.
